name: swap_masked_slot_with_global
description: Calls the memory release library routine three times in a loop, then follows a structure field to a memory slot. If the slot's masked value matches a fixed constant, it saves the slot's contents to a local, stores a global into the slot, and clears the global.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter held in a register in a tight loop until it reaches negative one, then returns. It touches no other state.

name: swap_aga_slot_with_global
description: Calls the memory release library routine three times in a loop, then follows a structure field to a memory slot. If the slot's masked value matches a different fixed constant, it saves the slot's contents, stores a global into the slot, and clears the global.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter held in a register in a tight loop until it reaches negative one, then returns. It touches no other state.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If the destination pointer argument is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in a base-register structure into that destination. It then calls a routine through a function pointer.

name: build_table_with_saved_words
description: Scans a linked list for its largest size value, then fills a block with an ascending sequence of values. It saves sixteen words into the block around library calls and restores them afterwards, returning zero on success and minus one when a library call yields zero.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If the destination pointer argument is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in a base-register structure into that destination. It then calls a routine through a function pointer.

description: Scans a linked list for its largest size value, then fills a block with an ascending sequence of values. It saves sixteen words into the block around library calls and restores them afterwards, returning zero on success and minus one when a library call yields zero.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If the destination pointer argument is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in a base-register structure into that destination. It then calls a routine through a function pointer.

name: parse_command_line_into_arguments
description: Allocates a control block and reads the command line of the running process. It splits the text into arguments on spaces and tabs, honours double-quoted text, and translates the escape codes star-N and star-E into newline and escape characters, storing argument pointers in the block.

name: find_fast_chip_memory_blocks
description: Walks the system memory list from a library base, selecting the first node in the fast address range with type five and the first chip-range node with type three. When both are found and differ, it calls two routines on them and then a third with the list head, the fast block and the chip block it points to.

name: build_table_with_saved_words
description: Scans a linked list for its largest size value, then fills a block with an ascending sequence of values. It saves sixteen words into the block around library calls and restores them afterwards, returning zero on success and minus one when a library call yields zero.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If the destination pointer argument is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in a base-register structure into that destination. It then calls a routine through a function pointer.

name: open_nil_or_parse_args
description: Allocates a control block and fills it from the process startup message or command line. When started from the Workbench it opens the NIL: device and keeps the handle in the block and process fields; otherwise it parses the command line into arguments. It then closes any handles it opened and returns zero, or one hundred when the block cannot be allocated.

name: close_handles_and_release_block
description: Stores the result value in a control block reached through the process task, then closes the handle, library and message-port resources recorded there when they are non-zero. It releases the block through a library call and returns the stored result.

name: launch_tool_or_report_error
description: Decodes obfuscated strings by XORing them with a fixed key byte, then looks up a resident module and opens the libraries it needs. It allocates a block, copies in the decoded text and starts the tool, and the referenced text shows it reports errors for a missing resident tag or a failed start.

name: compare_strings_ordered
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns minus one if the first byte is below the second, one if above, and zero when the strings are equal.

name: clone_list_with_lookup_values
description: Walks a chain of list entries, allocating an eight-byte node for each and storing a value obtained from a lookup routine in it. It links the nodes in order and returns the head, stopping early if an allocation or lookup returns zero.

name: call_library_vector_minus_132
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 132 from it, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: call_library_vector_minus_138
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 138 from it, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: match_workbench_release_and_pad
description: Checks whether the text at the given pointer begins with the fixed Workbench release string, and if the character at offset 20 is the digit two, writes a period and four spaces at offset 17 on a match. The referenced text is the Workbench release string, so the routine adjusts the version field.

name: write_version_field_padding
description: Writes a period followed by four spaces into five consecutive bytes of a buffer starting at offset 17. It fills a fixed-width field after the version text.

name: compare_prefix_with_global_text
description: Compares the text at the given pointer with a fixed global string one byte at a time. It stops as soon as the global string ends or a byte differs, and returns no value.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub. Calling it takes no action.

name: pass_args_with_stack_pointer
description: Passes its two incoming arguments to another routine together with the address of a stack slot, then returns. It keeps no result of its own.

name: format_text_and_pass_length
description: Calls a library formatting routine that writes text into a 140-byte stack buffer, then measures the buffer length up to its null terminator. If the length is non-zero, it passes the parameter, the buffer and the length to another routine.

name: parse_command_line_into_arguments
description: Allocates a control block and reads the command line of the running process. It splits the text into arguments on spaces and tabs, honours double-quoted text, and translates the escape codes star-N and star-E into newline and escape characters, storing argument pointers in the block.

name: release_control_block_with_result
description: Stores the result value in a control block reached through the process task, closes the library and message-port resources recorded there when they are non-zero, and releases the block. It returns the stored result.

name: check_library_version_from_args
description: Parses command-line arguments that name a library or device, with optional version, revision and unit numbers, and opens it to read its version and revision. It compares those against the requested minimums and prints Kickstart, Workbench, usage or open-error messages, as the referenced text shows.

name: call_routine_with_flag_128
description: Passes its first argument together with the constant 128 to another routine, then passes its second argument to a further routine and returns. It is a small wrapper that supplies a fixed flag value.

name: parse_integer_string
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign, then accumulates the decimal digits that follow into an integer. A minus sign negates the result, and any text after the digits is ignored.

name: compare_strings_ordered
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns minus one if the first byte is below the second, one if above, and zero when the strings are equal.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the bytes of a null-terminated string by scanning forward until the terminator, then returns that count.

name: reschedule_task_via_library
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 48 from it, which the library names identify as the task reschedule call. It passes no arguments.

name: dispatch_task_via_library
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 60 from it, which the library names identify as the task dispatch call. It passes no arguments.

name: pass_args_with_stack_pointer
description: Passes its two incoming arguments to another routine together with the address of a stack slot, then returns. It keeps no result of its own.

name: call_library_vector_minus_198
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 198 from it, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: call_library_vector_minus_414
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 414 from it, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: call_library_vector_minus_552
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 552 from it, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: format_text_and_pass_length
description: Calls a library formatting routine that writes text into a 140-byte stack buffer, then measures the buffer length up to its null terminator. If the length is non-zero, it passes the parameter, the buffer and the length to another routine.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register into the byte addressed by the address register. It is a single-instruction store helper with no other effect.

name: swap_ecs_slot_with_global
description: Calls the memory release library routine three times in a loop, then follows a structure field to a memory slot. If the slot's masked value matches a fixed constant, it saves the slot's contents, stores a global into the slot, and clears the global.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter held in a register in a tight loop until it reaches negative one, then returns. It touches no other state.

name: load_hunk_records_with_relocation
description: Walks AmigaDOS hunk records in a file image, allocating memory for each hunk and copying its contents into place. It applies relocation records by adding the hunk base address to each listed longword, and calls the library free routine in one branch.

name: busy_wait_word_counter
description: Counts a 16-bit register down through zero one step per pass until it wraps around once. It is a busy-wait delay with no calls and no other effect.

name: decompress_backward_lz_stream
description: Decodes a compressed byte stream read backwards from an end pointer. It reads flag bits, then copies either literal bytes or repeated runs from earlier output into the buffer until the start is reached, and stores the final output pointer in a global.

name: shift_multiword_value_with_carry
description: Performs a multi-precision shift across a sequence of words, reading each further word from memory as the shift proceeds. The count comes from a register, and the bits that move between words pass through the extend flag, one step per count value.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: This entry is bad data rather than code: the decompiler could not decode its instructions, and it ends in invalid bytes. No behaviour can be recovered from it.

name: unpack_rnc_tagged_blocks
description: After a memory allocation succeeds, walks a list of memory entries looking for one tagged with a signature of the letters R, N and C plus a version byte. It unpacks that entry's compressed blocks by copying them backwards with each word XORed against a rotating key, then frees the memory block.

name: extract_flag_bit_from_table
description: Scans a table of word pairs until one whose masked value matches the current key, then reads a byte from the matched entry. It checks a subtraction borrow to decide whether to call a further routine, then extracts one bit from a value table and sets that bit in the result.

name: mask_and_conditional_call
description: ANDs two 16-bit values together, then compares two byte values. If the first byte is less than the second, it calls another routine and returns that routine's word instead of the masked value.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub. Calling it takes no action.

name: build_canonical_code_table
description: Reads a symbol count and the bit length of each symbol into a stack buffer. It then assigns canonical codes ordered by bit length, bit-reverses each code, and writes the code, its length and derived mask values into a lookup table.

name: apply_relocation_records_with_base
description: Applies relocation records: when a record begins with the relocation tag, it clears that record, walks the memory list to the hunk index the record names, and adds that base address to each longword named by the record's offsets. Each entry is zeroed as it is consumed.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub. Calling it takes no action.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: This entry is bad data rather than code: the decompiler could not decode its instructions, and it ends in invalid bytes. No behaviour can be recovered from it.

name: toggle_bit_and_store_status
description: Partly decodes to a bit toggle and a comparison that stores a status word, but the instruction stream ends in bad data. The full behaviour cannot be recovered from this decompilation.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: This entry is bad data rather than code: the decompiler decoded a few stores but ends in invalid bytes. No reliable behaviour can be recovered from it.

name: calculate_scaled_table_offset
description: Multiplies a 16-bit argument by a 16-bit field from a structure, then adds a second 16-bit register value and a 32-bit field from the same structure. It returns the sum as a 32-bit value.

name: clear_word_field_after_call
description: Calls another routine, then writes zero to a 16-bit field of a structure reached through an address register. It has no return value.

name: shift_and_conditional_xor_word
description: Arithmetically shifts a 16-bit word right by one. When the original word's low bit is zero, it XORs the result with the low word of the second argument, then returns the 16-bit result.

name: xor_low_words
description: Returns the exclusive-or of the low word of the third argument with a 16-bit value from a register. The first two arguments are unused.

name: conditionally_call_by_flag_bits
description: Tests a 16-bit flag word: if it is below 16, or if bit 32 is set while one structure field is non-zero, or if bit 64 is set while another field is non-zero, it calls another routine. It always returns zero.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub. Calling it takes no action.

name: call_fixed_then_conditional
description: Calls another routine, then calls a fixed-address routine with two structure fields and the constant 11014. It calls a further routine only when a structure field is non-zero.

name: test_bit_in_indexed_table
description: Returns one when the low word argument is negative and zero when the high word is four or more. Otherwise it returns the bit selected by the two words from a byte table indexed by the same values.

name: test_table_bit_direct
description: Returns zero when the 16-bit index is four or more. Otherwise it returns the bit selected by the register pair from a byte table, the same lookup as the neighbouring routine without its negative check.

name: read_table_bit_unchecked
description: Returns the single bit selected by a 16-bit position from a byte table indexed by the other register, with no range check.

name: return_constant_100_status
description: Returns the constant one hundred and does nothing else. It is a fixed-status stub in the program entry of a font file.

name: return_constant_100_status
description: Returns the constant one hundred and does nothing else. It is a fixed-status stub in the program entry of a font file.

name: increment_counter_clear_bit
description: Library code that increments a 16-bit counter at one offset from a base pointer and clears the value 8 bit in a flag byte at another offset. It is part of the Icon library, not the game program.

name: decrement_library_refcount
description: Library code that decrements a 16-bit reference counter at one offset from the base pointer. When the counter reaches zero and the value 8 flag is set in a flag byte, it calls a cleanup routine and returns its result; otherwise it returns zero.

name: unlink_and_free_idle_node
description: Library code: if the counter at offset 8 is zero, it unlinks the node from its doubly linked list and releases its memory through the library free routine, returning the value saved from offset 42. Otherwise it sets the value 8 flag in a flag byte and returns zero.

name: set_pending_flag_return_zero
description: Library code that sets the value 8 flag in a flag byte at a fixed offset from the base pointer and returns zero.

name: open_resource_or_raise_alert
description: Library code that stores its incoming pointer and base in a structure, then calls a library routine at offset minus 408 to open a resource and records the returned handle. On failure it raises an alert through the system alert routine; on success it copies two stored pointers into global slots.

name: copy_two_pointers_from_table
description: Library code that copies two 32-bit values from fixed offsets of a structure addressed by a register into two global slots.

name: call_helper_then_return
description: Calls another routine and then returns, with no other operations. It is a pass-through wrapper in the Icon library.

name: store_value_in_returned_block
description: Library code that calls a library routine at offset minus 294 through a base pointer held in a structure, then stores the second argument into the returned block at offset 148. It performs this update and returns.

name: acquire_pointer_or_cleanup
description: Calls a helper with the last two arguments to obtain a pointer. If that pointer is non-null, it calls a second helper with it; when the second helper returns zero, it passes the pointer to a cleanup helper and returns zero, otherwise it returns the pointer.

name: load_icon_record_into_block
description: Looks up a record, then reads a second record into a local buffer and copies its ten words and several scalar fields into the first record at fixed offsets. If a linked field is non-zero it stores the record pointer there, and on failure it passes the record to a helper and returns zero.

name: store_stack_header_into_record
description: Library code that copies ten longwords from a stack header into a structure at offset 96, then copies several scalar fields into fixed offsets of the same structure. If the linked field at offset 76 is non-zero, it stores the structure pointer into that linked record.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns the constant zero and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: copy_icon_data_to_stack
description: Copies ten longwords from a structure at offset 96 into a local array, then copies several fields from the structure into other stack slots. It writes a fixed header word pair at the start of the stack block and calls another routine with the first two arguments and a pointer to that header.

name: load_info_file_record
description: Reads an icon file named with the referenced .info suffix into a local buffer. It checks that the first word is minus 7408 and the second word is one, then loads the record's fields and linked sub-records through allocating helpers; it returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: load_icon_records_from_header
description: Validates a header's magic word and revision, then reads its linked records and allocates memory for them through library calls, ending with a cleanup call. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: read_optional_icon_tables
description: Reads two values into a record and then loads optional tables from the stream. Each empty table slot is filled from a helper read, and one table is allocated and filled element by element; it returns one on success and zero on a failed read.

name: fill_array_then_read_slot
description: Fills a memory array element by element from helper reads until a counter in the caller's frame runs out, then reads one value into a record slot. It returns one on success and zero on any failed read.

name: return_zero_after_call
description: Calls another routine and then returns zero. It is a thin wrapper in the Icon library.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub in the Icon library. Calling it takes no action.

name: write_info_file_record
description: Allocates a 260-byte name buffer, builds a path from the given name and the referenced .info suffix, and opens the file for writing. It writes the record's header and optional tables through library calls, releases the buffer, and returns zero when a step fails.

name: write_icon_record_fields
description: Writes a record's header and optional string tables to an open file handle, then restores a saved field in the record. It returns the final write result, which is zero on failure.

name: write_icon_optional_tables
description: Writes the record's optional string fields: one string at offset 50, a null-terminated list of strings at offset 54 with each length written first, and one string at offset 70. It returns zero when any write fails.

name: write_string_list_with_count
description: Measures a null-terminated list of strings and writes its total size, then writes each entry and the string at offset 70. It returns zero when any write fails.

name: iterate_icon_table_entries
description: Walks a null-terminated list of strings, writing each entry's length and text, then writes the string at offset 70. It returns zero when a write fails.

name: process_linked_node_list
description: Walks a linked node list from a fixed offset in a structure, calling a helper on each node until the helper returns nothing or the sentinel is reached. It then calls the helper once more on the last node found.

name: iterate_linked_list_nodes
description: Calls a helper on the current node, follows the link to the next node through another helper call, and repeats until that helper returns nothing or the link at offset 8 returns to the list start. It then calls the helper once on the last node.

name: call_helper_with_offset_140
description: Calls another routine with the first argument unchanged and the second argument increased by 140, then returns.

name: allocate_cleared_icon_record
description: Allocates a cleared 168-byte block and calls a helper with a pointer 140 bytes into it. On success it calls a second helper with the block and returns the block; if the first helper fails it releases the block, and otherwise it returns zero.

name: call_helper_then_return
description: Calls another routine and then returns, with no other operations. It is a pass-through wrapper in the Icon library.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns the constant zero and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: store_pair_in_counted_buffer
description: Decrements a counter in a structure and, when it is exhausted, calls a helper to grow the buffer, returning zero if that fails. It then stores the two longword arguments into an eight-byte slot at the counter's index and returns one.

name: decrement_counter_and_store_pair
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter through a pointer, then stores two register values into the eight-byte slot at that index of a table found through a structure field. It returns one.

name: allocate_record_with_two_helpers
description: Allocates a cleared 94-byte block and calls a helper with a pointer 78 bytes into it. If the helpers succeed it returns the block; on failure it releases the block and returns zero.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub in the Icon library. Calling it takes no action.

name: call_library_routine_return_zero
description: Calls a library routine at offset minus 210 from a base pointer and then returns zero.

name: call_helper_with_offset_78
description: Calls another routine with the first argument unchanged and the second argument increased by 78, then returns.

name: find_value_after_equals_sign
description: Walks a null-terminated list of names, comparing each through a helper against a resolved string. When an entry matches and is followed by an equals sign, it returns the text after that sign, otherwise zero.

name: search_string_table_for_value
description: Scans a null-terminated table of string pointers, comparing each entry through a helper, and returns the text after the equals sign of the first matching entry. It returns zero when the table ends without a match.

name: search_pointer_list_for_value
description: Walks a null-terminated list of pointers, comparing each entry through a helper against a fixed string. For the first entry that matches and is followed by an equals sign, it returns the text after that sign, otherwise zero.

name: find_delimited_entry_match
description: Walks a list of entries separated by the bar character, comparing each entry's length and text with a candidate string through helpers. It returns one when an entry matches and zero when the list ends.

name: scan_delimited_entries_for_match
description: Walks the bar-delimited entries of a string, comparing the length and text of each with a candidate string through helpers. It returns one on the first match and zero when the string ends.

name: match_bar_delimited_entry
description: Steps through bar-separated entries, checking each entry's length and then its text against a candidate string through a helper. It returns one when an entry matches and zero when no entry remains.

name: match_entry_by_length
description: Steps through bar-separated entries, testing each entry's length against a target and then its text through a helper. It returns one on a full match and zero when the entries end.

name: scan_entries_by_length_match
description: Scans bar-separated entries by comparing their lengths with a target and, on equal length, confirming the text with a helper. It returns one when a match is found and zero at the end of the list.

name: parse_copy_prefix_and_number
description: Clears a 30-byte name field, then parses a copy-style name prefix such as copy or copy of, reading an optional decimal number after it. It writes the remaining text into the name field and returns the record pointer.

name: parse_copy_of_decimal_number
description: Checks for a fixed three-character word at offset five, parses a decimal number from the text after it, and confirms a following fixed four-character string. It makes two helper calls on either outcome and returns no value.

name: parse_decimal_then_check_suffix
description: Parses decimal digits from the text until a non-digit is found, then checks that the remaining text matches a fixed four-character string. It makes two helper calls on either outcome and returns no value.

name: accumulate_decimal_digits_check_tail
description: Accumulates decimal digits into a number as it reads them, then checks that the text after the digits matches a fixed four-character string. It makes two helper calls on either outcome and returns no value.

name: decimal_digit_value
description: Returns the numeric value of an ASCII decimal digit, or minus one when the character is not a digit.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns the constant minus one and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: call_library_vector_minus_198
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 198 from it, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: call_library_vector_minus_210
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 210 from it, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: acquire_pointer_or_cleanup
description: Calls a helper with the last two arguments to obtain a pointer. If that pointer is non-null, it calls a second helper with it; when the second helper returns zero, it passes the pointer to a cleanup helper and returns zero, otherwise it returns the pointer.

name: allocate_block_with_length
description: Allocates a cleared 96-byte block, sets its field at offset 14 to ten, and stores ten in the first word of the output buffer. It then passes the block to a helper with a pointer one word into that buffer, and returns true when the allocation succeeded.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns the constant zero and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: return_result_if_equal
description: Calls a helper with three arguments and returns its result when that result equals the fourth argument, otherwise zero.

name: return_result_if_equal
description: Calls a helper with three arguments and returns its result when that result equals the fourth argument, otherwise zero.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub in the Icon library. Calling it takes no action.

name: divide_32bit_by_divisor
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor. For divisors above 16 bits it uses a bit-by-bit shift and subtract loop; otherwise it divides the high and low halves in turn. It returns the remainder and quotient together in one 64-bit result.

name: restoring_division_16_steps
description: Performs sixteen shift-and-subtract steps on a 32-bit value, shifting each bit into a running remainder and subtracting the divisor when the remainder reaches it. The quotient and remainder are left in registers, and nothing is returned.

name: multiply_32bit_integers
description: Computes the low 32 bits of the product of two 32-bit register values using 16-bit partial products. It returns that product in the low word of the result.

name: call_raw_format_routine
description: Calls the text formatting library routine at offset minus 522 from a global base, passing no arguments and returning no value.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register into the byte addressed by the address register. It is a single-instruction store helper with no other effect.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the bytes of a null-terminated string by decrementing a counter for each byte until the terminator, then returns the count.

name: find_character_in_string
description: Scans a null-terminated string for a given character, returning a pointer to its first occurrence, or zero if the terminator is reached first.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns the constant zero and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies a null-terminated string from a source pointer to a destination pointer, byte by byte, including the terminator.

name: append_c_string
description: Advances to the terminator of the destination string, then copies the source string over that point byte by byte, including its terminator.

name: compare_strings_up_to_count
description: Compares two strings for up to a given count of bytes. It returns zero when they agree through the count or reach a shared terminator, and one at the first differing byte.

name: return_one_stub
description: Returns the constant one and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: scan_limited_string_then_call
description: Walks a string up to a given limit, stopping at its terminator. When the terminator is found it calls a helper, and it returns no value.

name: call_helper_then_return
description: Calls another routine and then returns, with no other operations. It is a pass-through wrapper in the Icon library.

name: copy_string_with_zero_padding
description: Copies a null-terminated string into a destination buffer for up to a given count of bytes, then fills any remaining count with zero bytes.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub in the Icon library. Calling it takes no action.

name: setup_pointer_chain
description: Initializes a list header in place: the first longword is set to point just past itself, the second is cleared, and the third points back to the header.

name: process_icon_request
description: Returns one when the argument is null. Otherwise it calls a helper with a size of 20 and, if that succeeds, makes two further helper calls, the last using a value read from offset 10 of the argument; it returns zero when the first helper fails.

name: walk_nodes_calling_helper_pair
description: Walks a linked list of nodes. For each node it calls one helper, then a second helper on the node's pointer with a size taken from a byte times four, and follows the next link; it returns one when the list ends and zero when a helper fails.

name: walk_nodes_until_failure
description: Follows a chain of nodes through the link at offset 12, calling two helpers on each node. It returns one when the chain ends and zero as soon as one helper fails.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns the constant zero and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: allocate_and_init_icon_node
description: Allocates a cleared 20-byte block through a helper when the flag argument is non-zero. It then calls two helpers, storing the second result at offset 10 of the block; it returns the block on success and minus one on failure, or zero when the flag is zero.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns the constant minus one and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: build_icon_node_chain
description: Builds a chain of cleared 16-byte nodes, linking each to the previous one. For each node it allocates a further block whose size is a byte from the node times four, stores it at offset 8, and fills it through a helper. It returns the first node, or minus one when any step fails.

name: walk_and_link_node_chain
description: Repeatedly obtains a node from a helper, links it to the previous node at offset 12, and stores a second helper result at offset 8 before continuing to the next node. It returns the first node, or minus one if any step fails.

name: build_node_list_from_helpers
description: Builds a list of nodes by repeatedly obtaining a node from a helper and storing a second helper result at offset 8 of each node, linking nodes at offset 12. It returns the first node, or minus one when any step fails.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns the constant minus one and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Icon library.

name: check_and_set_font_handle
description: Calls a library routine at offset minus 84 from the base. If it returns a non-zero handle, it stores the argument at offset 34 of that handle and calls a second library routine at offset minus 396, and it returns whether a handle was obtained.

name: check_and_set_font_handle
description: Calls a library routine at offset minus 84 from the base. If it returns a non-zero handle, it stores the argument at offset 34 of that handle and calls a second library routine at offset minus 396, and it returns whether a handle was obtained.

name: open_libraries_and_init_list
description: Opens two system libraries and, if both open, initialises a list header inside the given structure so that it points just past itself, then returns the structure. If either open fails, it closes the first library where needed, releases the structure, and returns zero.

name: close_library_and_free_block
description: Closes a library through the library base and releases the structure through the memory free routine, then returns zero.

name: release_unused_font_entries
description: Walks a list of font entries, unlinking each one whose count is not positive and unloading its segment through a library routine, then decrements the owner's count. If no references remain and the owner's flag is clear, it closes two libraries, releases the owner block and returns its stored handle; otherwise it sets the value 128 flag and returns zero.

name: close_font_handle_if_unused
description: If both counters are zero or below, it closes two libraries, releases the block, unlinks it from its list and returns its stored handle. Otherwise it sets the value 128 flag in the flag byte and returns zero.

name: set_flag_and_return_zero
description: Sets the value 128 flag in a flag byte of the structure and returns zero.

name: empty_return_stub
description: This routine contains only a return instruction with no effect, so it is a stub in the Diskfont library. Calling it takes no action.

name: clear_flag_and_increment_counter
description: Clears the value 128 flag in a flag byte of the structure and increments a 16-bit counter at a fixed offset in the same structure.

name: release_counter_when_idle
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter in a structure and, when it reaches zero with the value 128 flag set, calls a library routine at offset minus 18 and returns its result. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: build_font_entry_buffer
description: Fills a buffer with font entries: for each font record in a linked list it copies the name, a size word and two style bytes into a fixed-size table. When bit 2 of the flags is set it also adds entries found by scanning the font directory, and it returns the negated shortfall, or zero when everything fit.

name: copy_fonts_then_scan_dir
description: Adds font records from a linked list into a table as name, size and style entries, then, when bit 2 of the flags is set, scans the font directory and adds matching entries the same way. It returns the negated shortfall, or zero when everything fit.

name: copy_font_names_into_buffer
description: Copies the characters of each font name into a buffer and adds a table entry for it, walking a linked list of font records. It returns the negated shortfall, or zero when everything fit.

name: scan_fonts_directory_entries
description: Reads the fonts directory through the dos directory calls, using the text FONTS: as the location. It adds the entries it finds to the table and returns the negated shortfall, or zero when everything fit.

name: scan_font_files_for_entries
description: Scans directory entries and keeps those whose name ends with the referenced .font suffix. It opens each matching file through the dos Open call and adds it to the table with its name, size and style, returning the negated shortfall or zero.

name: append_font_name_entries
description: Copies the characters of a name into the buffer at a moving position, then adds a table entry for it, repeating over the names it reads. It returns the negated shortfall, or zero when everything fit.

name: read_font_directory_entries
description: Reads font file entries through the dos read call, copying each name into the buffer and adding a table entry, and repeats until no further entries are returned. It returns the negated shortfall, or zero when everything fit.

name: scan_font_directory_with_locks
description: Walks the font directory with the dos lock, examine-next and unlock calls, adding a table entry for each matching file name. When the scan finishes it releases its memory block through the free routine, and it returns the negated shortfall, or zero when everything fit.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns the constant zero and does nothing else. It is a stub in the Diskfont library.

name: score_font_style_difference
description: Scores a font record against a target: if its 16-bit field is zero it returns minus 32767, otherwise it starts from a size difference and subtracts a table weight for each differing bit in two style bytes across seven bit positions.

name: sum_style_bit_differences
description: Starts from a value adjusted by a 16-bit field and subtracts a table weight for each differing bit of two style byte pairs over seven bit positions. It returns the total.

name: subtract_weighted_style_bits
description: Walks seven bit positions of a mask, subtracting a table weight for each position whose bit is set in a style byte, and returns the remaining value.

name: subtract_style_weights_by_mask
description: Walks seven bit positions, subtracting a table weight from a starting value for each position that is set in a mask, and returns the result.

name: return_constant_value
description: Returns the fixed 32-bit value minus 32767 without using any arguments or registers.

name: find_best_font_and_add
description: Scores fonts in the fonts directory against a requested font descriptor and picks the best-scoring entry. It opens the chosen font through the graphics open-font call and records it in the font list, returning the matched record, or the existing one when no better match exists.

name: lock_fonts_dir_add_best
description: Locks the fonts directory with the dos lock call and reads the file entries it finds, repeatedly selecting the best-scoring entry against the requested font and adding it to the font list. It returns the last record added, or zero when none was.

name: read_fonts_add_best
description: Reads font file entries through the dos open, read and lock calls, repeatedly choosing the best-scoring entry against the requested font and adding it to the font list. It returns the last record added, or zero when none was.

name: add_best_scoring_font_entries
description: Repeatedly chooses the best-scoring entry from a set of font records against the requested font, and adds each chosen entry to the font list. It returns the last record added, or zero when none was.

name: add_fonts_to_graphics
description: Repeatedly chooses the best-scoring font record and adds each chosen one to the graphics font list through the add-font routine, using the current-directory, parent-directory and load-segment calls along the way. It returns the last record added, or zero when none was.

name: unload_font_segments_and_release
description: Repeatedly chooses the best-scoring font record, clears its slot, and unloads the font's segment through the dos unload call when one is loaded. It returns the last record that remained, or zero.

name: scan_release_best_fonts
description: Repeatedly chooses the best-scoring font record, adding records to the list and clearing slots that are empty. It then releases its directory lock, handle, memory block and any opened font through the unlock, close, free and close-font calls, and returns the last record that remained, or zero.

name: build_font_file_table
description: Scans the fonts directory with the dos lock, examine and current-directory calls, and keeps names ending in the referenced .font suffix. It allocates a cleared table with one 260-byte entry per matching file, records each entry's name, size and style fields, and returns the table, or zero when a step fails.
